sentences.text: Megavitiornis altirostris was an extinct, flightless, giant bird that lived only in Fiji.
The specific name altirostris highlights the bird's exceptionally tall vertical beak.
Its large body size, reduced shoulder bones, and missing breast keel all indicate it could not fly.
The beak was extraordinarily deep, measuring twenty-eight percent of the total length.
This species was likely the largest bird in Fiji during its time.
Scientists speculate the bird used its massive beak to crack hard seeds from large forest fruits.
The genus is monotypic, meaning it contains only this single known species.
Trevor Worthy formally described the genus in the year 2000.
Fossil remains have been found in caves on Viti Levu and Naigani Island.
Researchers suggest Megavitiornis likely went extinct due to overhunting by humans after they colonized Fiji.
Recent studies place Megavitiornis in the family Sylviornithidae, outside the Galliformes crown group, related to Sylviornis.
The parent group of the genus Megavitiornis is Sylviornithidae.
Fossils of Megavitiornis date to the Holocene epoch.
Megavitiornis lived from the Late Pleistocene to the Holocene, between 0.129 and 0 million years ago.
